instructions: Rinse the spinach in a big bowl of cold water and lift it into a colander. Shake it well and leave it to drain while you chop. Wet spinach turns the curry watery.
Finely chop the onion and the 2 tomatoes. Mince the 2 garlic cloves and grate 1 tsp of the ginger. Cut the paneer into 1 inch cubes.
Seed and thinly slice the green chili and put it in a small bowl for the table.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium high. Add the paneer in a single layer and leave it for about 2 minutes, until the underside is light golden. Turn the pieces and cook the other sides for another 2 minutes, then move them to a plate.
Turn the heat down to medium and add another 1 tbsp of the oil and the 1/4 cup cashews. Add the spinach a few handfuls at a time and stir for 3 to 4 minutes, until it's all wilted and dark green.
Tip the spinach and cashews into a blender and leave them to cool for 5 minutes. Add 1/2 cup water and blend to a smooth, thick puree. Add a tablespoon or two more water if the blades get stuck.

Wipe out the skillet and set it over medium heat. Melt 2 tbsp of the butter with the last 1 tbsp of oil, then add the 1/4 tsp cumin seeds, the 2 cardamom pods, the 2 cloves and the cinnamon stick. After about 30 seconds they'll sizzle and smell warm.
Add the onion and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's soft and golden at the edges.
Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook for about 1 minute, until they smell fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and the 1 tsp salt. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until the tomatoes break down and turn mushy.
Stir in the 1 tsp garam masala and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until it smells toasty.
Pour in 1 cup water, cover the pan and simmer on low for 5 to 6 minutes, until the onion is completely soft. There should still be a little water in the pan.

Crush the 1 tsp kasuri methi between your palms over the pan and pour in the spinach puree. Stir and cook on low for 2 to 3 minutes, until it starts to bubble. Add a splash of hot water if it's thicker than you like. Don't cook it longer than that, or the spinach turns a dull olive green.
Stir in the paneer and 1/4 cup of the cream and warm it through for 1 minute. Take the pan off the heat and pick out the cinnamon stick. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with naan or basmati rice, with the sliced chili on the side.
method_notes: All three versions cook an onion, ginger, garlic and tomato masala and stir in a spinach puree and paneer at the end, finished with cream and kasuri methi. Swasthi's (the lead) sautes the spinach with cashews and green chilies before blending and blooms cinnamon, cardamom, cloves and cumin in butter first. Cook with Manali blanches the spinach and blends it raw with tomato, garlic and ginger, then adds turmeric, chili powder and a squeeze of lemon. RecipeTin Eats blends only half the spinach and pan fries the paneer until golden. This one follows Swasthi's method with a little more spinach, browns the paneer the RecipeTin way, and moves the green chili to the table to keep the pot mild.
